title: v1.9 independent blinded re-rating of emulation quality (step 1)
blinding: Rated from the RULE DEFINITIONS section of docs/v17/TRIAL_SELECTION_RULE.md (lines 1-35), trial_specs.py design fields, rct_facts.json, candidate caveats and published protocols, before opening docs/v17/trial_selection.json or the rule's per-trial table. No emulation result was viewed. Disclosure: a grep of docs/paper/table1_picot.md displayed its 'Emulation quality' class column, and trial_specs.py displayed older v1.3 RATING_ITEMS tuples; neither per-item rating was used.
rule: F1-F5 core flags (0/1); comparator and outcome fidelity good/moderate/poor, as defined in TRIAL_SELECTION_RULE.md section 1.

trials.rationale: Apixaban vs warfarin initiators in outpatient AF; stroke/SE from inpatient codes. VKA-experienced patients transitioned by protocol (post-randomisation washout), which RCT-DUPLICATE did not score as baseline-therapy discontinuation.
sources: Wang et al. JAMA 2023;329:1376, Table 2 (RCT-DUPLICATE design-difference ratings)

trials.rationale: Same agents; ITT benchmark; stroke/SE from inpatient codes; VKA transition handled as for ARISTOTLE.
sources: Wang et al. JAMA 2023;329:1376, Table 2 (RCT-DUPLICATE design-difference ratings)

trials.rationale: Dabigatran vs warfarin; the benchmark is the 150 mg arm and 110 mg is not marketed in the US (75 mg only below RE-LY's CrCl limit), so the agent and effective dose match; stroke/SE from inpatient codes.
sources: Wang et al. JAMA 2023;329:1376, Table 2 (RCT-DUPLICATE design-difference ratings)

trials.rationale: Horizon 61 mo (F4). Early rhythm-control strategy approximated by adding an antiarrhythmic (ablation-first not captured). Composite needs CV death from listed causes and HF/ACS hospitalisation codes.
Horizon 49 mo (F4). RCT drug arm = rate or rhythm drugs; emulation = antiarrhythmic initiators. 'Disabling' stroke not identifiable; serious bleeding reduced to GI bleed/ICH hospitalisation.
Sequential add-on design mirrors adding rhythm control to rate control; strategy approximated by antiarrhythmic initiation (cardioversion not captured). All-cause death.
Same strategy approximation as AFFIRM in HFrEF. Primary endpoint CV death needs listed causes of death.

Sequential warfarin-to-DOAC switch mirrors the randomised switch (F3 not flagged); any DOAC as in the trial. Primary = major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding; CRNM bleeding (the dominant component) is not ascertainable, only major-bleeding hospitalisation.

Occlusion vs none at the same cardiac surgery; time zero is the surgery in both arms (F1 not flagged). Ischaemic stroke/SE from codes, but perioperative (index-stay) events, part of the RCT primary, are not counted.
LAAO vs continued warfarin in OAC-treated AF (sequential; no future information). Composite includes CV/unexplained death needing listed causes.
Ablation vs continued rate control; comparator antiarrhythmic use not excluded (contamination of the rate-control strategy). HF events from any-position HF hospitalisation codes.

77% were on OAC at entry and the clopidogrel+aspirin arm stopped it at randomisation (no protocol transition window); the initiator design neither requires nor reproduces that OAC discontinuation (F3). Aspirin not identifiable. Composite includes vascular death.
sources: ACTIVE Writing Group, Lancet 2006 (PMID 16765759): prior OAC 77%

trials.rationale: Horizon 58 mo (F4). Carvedilol vs immediate-release metoprolol tartrate, as in the RCT (docs/COMET_ADAPTED_PROTOCOL.md); dose not identifiable (record-only titration). All-cause death.

Sequential enalapril then sacubitril/valsartan active run-in removed intolerant patients (F2). The ACEi/ARB switch is mirrored by the sequential switch design. Comparator = any ACEi (trial: enalapril). CV death or HF hospitalisation.
sources: Wang et al. JAMA 2023;329:1376, Table 2 (RCT-DUPLICATE design-difference ratings)

trials.rationale: Randomised before discharge from an HF admission; initiators within 30 d of an HF code can take time zero from an inpatient IV furosemide order vs an oral discharge torsemide strategy (F1). 67% were on a loop diuretic before admission and changed agent at randomisation; the new-user design excludes them (F3). All-cause death.
Class adaptation (any ARB vs any ACEi; trial losartan vs captopril) in ACEi-naive HF; 18 mo; all-cause death.
Placebo-controlled RCT emulated with a DPP-4i active-comparator proxy (estimand changes); T2D restriction. CV death or HF hospitalisation.

Horizon 58 mo (F4). ARB class vs cardioselective beta-blocker class (trial losartan vs atenolol). Prior therapy was withdrawn during a placebo run-in before randomisation (not F2/F3). CV death, MI or stroke.

About 90% were treated at entry and prior antihypertensives were replaced by study drug at randomisation without washout; initiator design does not mirror this (F3). Horizon 59 mo (F4). Thiazide class for chlorthalidone. Fatal CHD needs listed causes.

89.9% previously treated were switched directly to study drug without run-in (F3). Horizon 50 mo (F4). ARB class for valsartan. Cardiac composite approximated by CV death, HF hospitalisation and MI (emergency procedures not captured).
sources: Julius et al. Lancet 2004; Hypertension 2006 VALUE review

trials.rationale: Previously treated patients (most) had therapy replaced at randomisation (PROBE, no washout) (F3). Horizon 66 mo (F4). Atenolol-based strategy approximated by cardioselective beta-blocker initiation. Fatal CHD from listed causes; silent MI not captured.
4-week placebo run-in (washout) before randomisation, not flagged. Nifedipine (GITS not identifiable) vs thiazide class for co-amilozide. Composite needs CV death and HF hospitalisation codes.
sources: Brown et al. Lancet 2000 (4-week placebo run-in)

trials.rationale: P2Y12 inhibitors in ACS start within the index admission and EHR inpatient orders are visible (F1 exemption in the rule). Vascular death needs listed causes.
sources: Wang et al. JAMA 2023;329:1376, Table 2 (RCT-DUPLICATE design-difference ratings)

trials.rationale: RCT randomised 0.5-10 d after MI in hospital; ACEi/ARB are started in the admission with visible inpatient orders (treated like the P2Y12 exemption; borderline). Class adaptation (valsartan vs captopril). All-cause death.
Placebo-controlled; DPP-4i proxy. 3-point MACE with CV death from listed causes.
sources: Wang et al. JAMA 2023;329:1376, Table 2 (RCT-DUPLICATE design-difference ratings)

trials.rationale: Same agents (linagliptin vs glimepiride). Horizon 76 mo (F4). Prior SU/glinide was stopped at randomisation for a minority (SU-exposed stratum); not judged substantial (RCT-DUPLICATE: no). 3-point MACE.
sources: Wang et al. JAMA 2023;329:1376, Table 2 (RCT-DUPLICATE design-difference ratings)
Marx et al. Diab Vasc Dis Res 2015 (PMC4390606)

trials.rationale: Placebo-controlled; DPP-4i proxy. Horizon 46 mo (<48). 3-point MACE.
sources: Wang et al. JAMA 2023;329:1376, Table 2 (RCT-DUPLICATE design-difference ratings)

trials.rationale: Placebo-controlled; DPP-4i proxy. 3-point MACE.
Placebo-controlled; DPP-4i proxy. Horizon 65 mo (F4). 3-point MACE.
Placebo-controlled; DPP-4i proxy. Horizon 50 mo (F4). CV death or HF hospitalisation.
sources: Wang et al. JAMA 2023;329:1376, Table 2 (RCT-DUPLICATE design-difference ratings)

trials.rationale: Placebo-controlled; DPP-4i proxy. Horizon 43 mo. 3-point MACE.
sources: Wang et al. JAMA 2023;329:1376, Table 2 (RCT-DUPLICATE design-difference ratings)

trials.rationale: Placebo-controlled; sulfonylurea proxy (rated poor in RCT-DUPLICATE). 4-point MACE incl. UA hospitalisation.
sources: Wang et al. JAMA 2023;329:1376, Table 2 (RCT-DUPLICATE design-difference ratings)

trials.rationale: Placebo-controlled; sulfonylurea proxy. 3-point MACE.
sources: Wang et al. JAMA 2023;329:1376, Table 2 (RCT-DUPLICATE design-difference ratings)

trials.rationale: 3-week single-blind active run-in (ramipril, then telmisartan+ramipril) removed intolerant patients (F2 as the rule defines it). Horizon 56 mo (F4). ARB class for telmisartan, ACEi class for ramipril. CV death, MI, stroke or HF hospitalisation.
Same agents (celecoxib vs naproxen; OTC naproxen unseen, dose titration record-only). APTC composite needs CV death incl. haemorrhagic.

Apixaban vs warfarin (with parenteral lead-in) after acute VTE; both started around the index encounter with visible orders. Recurrent VTE from a new inpatient stay with a VTE code: ascertainable but low specificity and outpatient-managed recurrences missed (moderate, as RCT-DUPLICATE rated its AMPLIFY outcome).
sources: Wang et al. JAMA 2023;329:1376, Table 2 (RCT-DUPLICATE design-difference ratings)

trials.rationale: Rosuvastatin vs atorvastatin (factorial with intensity strategy; agents match). Any coronary revascularisation, the most frequent component of the RCT composite, is not captured (dominant component missing).

The tested hypothesis is intensive (atorvastatin 80) vs moderate (pravastatin 40) therapy; dose is not identifiable, so atorvastatin initiators at any dose change the hypothesis. Revascularisation >= 30 d, the most frequent component, is not captured. Statins start in the ACS admission (F1 not flagged).
